text: The 'One Over Many' argument is offered in support of which conclusion?
choices: There are universals, entities that can be wholly present in many distinct particulars, because distinct things can genuinely be the same way.
There are only particulars, since apparent sameness is just the application of a shared predicate.
Properties are particular tropes rather than universals, unified only by resemblance.
There is a distinct property corresponding to every meaningful predicate whatsoever.
explanation: The One Over Many infers a shared universal from the premise that numerically distinct particulars can be genuinely the same way (same color, kind). The tempting distractor (option 1) is the predicate-nominalist denial of the argument's second premise, which is a rejection of the argument, not its conclusion.
